title: Cohort Launch: Assessment Framework + Day Zero Onboarding Kit
content:
Purpose:
This doc outlines a lightweight, repeatable framework to hire and onboard small engineering cohorts (3–8 hires) in a single wave. It bundles: (A) a calibrated assessment and interview rubric tuned for fast decisions at scale, and (B) a Day Zero + Week 0 micro-onboarding kit to maximize time-to-first-impact.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: people-ops, hiring managers, interviewers (eng/product/sre), hiring coordinators, and onboarding mentors.
- Scope: mid‑level ICs (L3–L4) across platform, serving runtime, and developer-experience teams. This is intentionally compact — for larger cohorts or senior hires use the extended playbook.

High-level goals:
1) Reduce calendar churn: consistent 3‑step interview funnel (take-home + 60m deep dive + behavioral capstone).
2) Speedy calibration: shared rubric and scoring normalization to make hire/no-hire decisions within 7 business days.
3) Smooth Day Zero: checklist-driven onboarding that gets engineers contributing to a low-risk task by EOW.

Funnel overview (ideal timeline):
- Day 0: Application screens and take-home sent within 48 hours of resume screen.
- Day 3–5: Take-home returns; 60-minute technical interview scheduled.
- Day 6–7: Behavioral / partnership interview + hiring committee review.
- Day 7–10: Offer or no-offer.

Assessment components (weights):
- Take-home project (40%): short (3–5 hour) scoped exercise that mirrors a tiny slice of the role. Graded against rubric below.
- Technical deep-dive (30%): 60m interview focusing on system design, debugging, and tradeoffs.
- Collaboration & impact (20%): behavioral interview targeted at cross-team work, shipping, and on-call judgement.
- Cultural fit & growth (10%): alignment with Redwood values and learning orientation.

Scoring rubric (1–5 per axis; 5 = exceptional):
- Correctness & craft: code quality, tests, edge-case handling.
- Design & systems sense: architecture choices, performance/cost tradeoffs.
- Debugging & reasoning: problems solved during live interview, clarity of thought.
- Communication & collaboration: clarity, empathy, deference to data.
- Ownership & delivery: evidence of shipping and iterating in past projects.

Normalization and decision policy:
- Panel average >= 4.3: strong hire (auto-approve fast-track).
- Average 3.5–4.3: hire with manager sign-off after calibration check.
- Average < 3.5: decline or recommend re‑engage after 6 months.
- At least one score 2 or below triggers a focused follow-up from hiring manager to validate edge-case concerns.

Take-home exercises (role-specific examples):
- Serving Runtime (L3): "latency-tracer" — implement a tiny RPC tracer that aggregates per-endpoint latencies and returns a percentile summary. Requirements: clear README, edge-case tests, and a short note on batching tradeoffs. (3–5 hours)
- Platform Engineering (L3): "quota-sim" — design and implement a simple quota evaluator for simulated requests. Provide a short runbook describing how you'd monitor violations. (2–4 hours)
- Developer Experience (L3): "sdk-smoke" — add an input validation layer to a toy SDK and supply unit tests + usage snippet demonstrating error messages. (2–3 hours)

Interview question bank (examples):
- System design: "Design an autoscaling pool for model inference where cold-start latency must be < 200ms for 95% of requests. What metrics, fallback tiers, and routing policies would you implement?"
- Debugging: "You see a sudden 2x increase in p50 latency on a single model. Walk through your incident triage steps."
- Behavioral: "Describe a time you pushed back on a shipped tradeoff. How did you communicate and what was the outcome?"

Interviewer guidance and calibration tips:
- Use the rubric language verbatim when taking notes; avoid qualitative-only comments (e.g., write: ‘Design: 3 — missed cache invalidation and no latency budget’).
- Identify one clear strength and one area of risk per candidate in your comment.
- If you're unsure between two adjacent scores, favor the lower score and annotate why. Hiring managers will adjudicate borderline cases.

Day Zero onboarding checklist (pre-boarding actions prior to 09:00 first day):
- IT & access:
  - AD account created, SSO invited, MFA required (IT).
  - LDAP group membership for pod added.
  - VPN/VPC access and dev cluster credentials provisioned.
  - Local workstation image (mac/linux) request submitted; dev container image link shared.
- Admin & HR:
  - Offer paperwork complete and benefits orientation scheduled.
  - Payroll and tax forms returned.
- Role & mentorship:
  - Manager assigned first-week 1:1 slots and weekly mentor pairing created.
  - First 2-week project and low-risk PR assigned (owner + acceptance criteria).
- Communication & tools:
  - Slack channels pre-joined (#team, #pod-oncall, #new-hires).
  - Access to repo read/write for assigned project and CI pipelines verified.
  - Calendar invite for Week 0 sync + orientation saved.

Day Zero run-of-day (first business day agenda):
- 09:00–09:30: Welcome + cohort intro (people-ops).
- 09:30–10:30: IT walkthrough and developer environment setup (dev-ops buddy).
- 10:30–12:00: Readme + tiny starter task assigned and paired coding session.
- 12:00–13:00: Team lunch (virtual or onsite).
- 13:00–14:00: Product/architecture overview (pod tech lead).
- 14:00–16:00: First PR attempt: small change to docs/tests; mentor review.
- 16:00–17:00: End-of-day sync + feedback survey (people-ops)

Week 0 microplan (first 5 business days):
- Goal: merged low-risk PR and successful run of CI + one local integration test.
- Day 1–2: ramp documents, local dev environment, repo walkthrough.
- Day 3: shadow on-call rotation and incident postmortem reading.
- Day 4: pair on feature/enhancement; open PR.
- Day 5: PR merged + 30m retrospective with mentor and manager.

Mentor playbook (15–30 minutes daily):
- Morning check: unblock list (what'll you do today?).
- Afternoon review: PR feedback + focused learning topic for next day.
- End-of-week: update competency log (linked to performance onboarding rubric).

Candidate experience & comms cadence (example templates):
- After resume screen: "Thanks — we've sent a short take-home to complete in 72 hours."
- After technical interview: brief summary + timeline for next steps (within 48 hours).
- Post-offer: warm handoff to people-ops with Day Zero checklist and benefits orientation link.

Metrics and signals to track for improvements:
- Time-to-offer (target: <= 10 business days for cohort hires).
- Offer acceptance rate (target: >= 80% for cohort offers).
- First-week activation: percent merged PR by EOW (target: >= 75%).
- New hire satisfaction: Day 1 NPS-style pulse (target: >= 7/10).

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: take-home fatigue deters applicants. Mitigation: keep exercises <5 hours and provide a clear rubric and example solution.
- Risk: interview panel overload during cohort window. Mitigation: pre-book rotating interviewer blocks and use pairing interviewers where possible.
- Risk: Day Zero access delays. Mitigation: require IT provisioning 5 business days before start date and a verification checklist 48 hours prior.

Open items and next steps:
- Finalize take-home templates for each role (owners: Daniel Park / Aisha Khan).
- Create a small library of anonymized exemplar take-home solutions for interviewer calibration.
- Run a pilot cohort in Q1 2026 and capture metrics to iterate on time-to-offer and Day 1 activation.

Appendix: quick evaluation cheat-sheet (one-pager for interviewers)
- Reminder: use 1–5 scale; write one-line strength and risk; submit within 24 hours.
- Calibration anchor examples: 5 = clearly exceeds on multiple axes with robust tradeoff discussion; 3 = competent but missing edge-case thinking; 1–2 = concerning gaps in core skills.

Contact and owners:

- Hiring process leads: Daniel Park (engineering hiring), Aisha Khan (onboarding program)
- Escalations: Marco Ruiz (Head of People Ops)
